problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(0,-4),(1,0),(2,-3).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under a counterclockwise rotation of ${30}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(2,-2\sqrt{3})$
- $(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2},\frac{1}{2})$
- $(4,-4\sqrt{3})$

feedback.problem:
A triangle $S$ has vertices at $(-2,-2),(0,4),(2,-2).$ Which of the following are coordinates of the vertices of ${S}^{′},$ the image of $S$ under a counterclockwise rotation of ${45}^{∘}$ about the origin?

- $(0,-2\sqrt{2})$
- $(1,-\sqrt{3})$
- $(2\sqrt{2},0)$
feedback.worked_solution:
The rotation matrix ${R}_{\theta }$ represents a rotation of angle $\theta $ counterclockwise about the origin and is given by

$$
{R}_{\theta }=[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  & -\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  & \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \end{aligned}].
$$

Substituting $\theta ={45}^{∘}$ into the above, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}R & =[\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘}) & -\operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}) \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡({45}^{∘}) & \operatorname{cos}⁡({45}^{∘})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & -\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} & \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

To find the image of $S$ under the transformation, we first create a matrix $X$ containing all of the vertices of $S:$

$$
\begin{aligned}X & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the image of $X$ under the rotation $R$ by calculating the matrix product $RX:$

$$
\begin{aligned}RX & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}[\begin{aligned}0 & -4 & 4 \\ -4 & 4 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -2\sqrt{2} & 2\sqrt{2} \\ -2\sqrt{2} & 2\sqrt{2} & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the coordinates of the respective vertices of ${S}^{′}$ are 

$$
(0,-2\sqrt{2}),\,(-2\sqrt{2},2\sqrt{2}),\,(2\sqrt{2},0).
$$

So, the correct answer is "I and III only."
